root_idea.summary: The root centers on the palate and mouth, extending by analogy to acts that reach, consume, control, or bring something to its furthest extent.
root_idea.development: From the physical palate and mouth come the senses of eating, bridling, and the beak; figurative developments include consuming something completely, gaining mastery over it, reaching maturity through experience, and understanding something thoroughly.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect-tense dictionary citation اِحْتَنَكَ.

senses.definition: To consume, extirpate, or destroy completely.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic threat, the verb is understood figuratively from consuming or exhausting something until nothing remains; it is one interpretation of the threat against the progeny of Adam.

senses.definition: To gain mastery over, subjugate, or lead as with a bridle.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, the verb may describe bringing the progeny under control, leading them to obedience, or figuratively bridling them. This is an alternative interpretation of the same threat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rub a child's palate with chewed dates or a similar substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The resulting child may be called مَحْنُوكٌ or مُحَنَّكٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rub or strike the palate with an object so as to make it bleed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The described use includes inserting a piece of wood into a beast's upper palate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mature firmness and soundness of judgment produced by age, experience, or the management of affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In related verbal and participial uses, experience or affairs make a person seasoned, experienced, disciplined, or tractable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To understand a thing thoroughly and master it.
To turn someone back or away from an affair.
To turn or tuck a cloth beneath the chin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use includes arranging a portion of a turban beneath the chin and turning a corpse's grave cloth beneath the lower jaw.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat vehemently or voraciously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description particularly concerns eating strongly after having eaten little or feebly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be pulled up by the roots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of trees or woody vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The palate or the region beneath the chin and lower jaw; by extension, the mouth or a bird's beak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer to the upper palate, lower mouth region, both jaws, or, in a bird, the beak.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely black.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions such as أَسْوَدُ حَانِكٌ; حَنَكُ الغُرَابِ may refer to the crow's beak or, figuratively, its intense blackness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A party of people seeking herbage in a district in order to pasture their animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a tropical plural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intelligent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence applies this designation to both women and men.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Eaters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a designation for men in the cited plural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thong or piece of wood joining parts of a saddle frame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object joins the wooden components of a riding saddle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bond or restraint for the neck, used to bind a captive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By extension, the expression أَخَذَ بِحِنَاكِ صَاحِبِهِ describes seizing someone by the chin and chest and dragging him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old man.
Niggardly, tenacious, or avaricious.
A good eater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a beast, including a she-camel or sheep or goat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The most voracious, or more voracious, of a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited comparisons apply to camels and to sheep or goats; the form is treated as an anomalous superlative for this natural attribute.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A string used to tie up a corpse's lower jaw.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Passive result of the palate-rubbing action already represented.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence in 17:62 has two directly attested lexical interpretations: complete extirpation/ destruction and gaining mastery or leading as with a bridle. The supplied contextual English rendering reflects the first interpretation.
The public headword اِحْتَنَكَ is the normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form; the supplied Quran occurrence is an imperfect Form VIII form.
